label: verify-bm-hydrogels

claims.claim: PEGDMA-600 with 1 wt% TPO printed on a Formlabs Form 2 at 405 nm, gel fraction 97.6%, giving a Formlabs hydrogel precedent.
claims.source_says: The 3D printing machine utilised was the Formlabs Form 2 SLA ... 250 mW laser at a 405 nm ... results of 99.33% and 97.58% for the UV chamber and SLA samples, respectively.
claims.note: All parts are in the paper; that TPO was the initiator for the SLA samples is an inference from its either/or wording.

claims.claim: LCD-printed GelMA bilayer strips bent to radii of 11-20 mm, linear swelling 7.83% at 30 s down to 0.70% at 70 s, E about 15-20 kPa; project Timoshenko ceiling predicts about 11 mm.
claims.source_says: radii of curvature between 11 and 20 mm depending on the geometry; Table 1: 30 s swelling 7.83%, 70 s 0.70%, modulus 14.48 to 20.23 kPa.
claims.note: Paper figures match; the 10.9-11.0 mm prediction is the agent's own calculation, and calcs.py does print R_min=10.9 mm, but the text of the paper gives 7.7% and about 1% in prose, differing slightly from the table.

claims.claim: Printed PEG-acrylate swelling is tunable from about 0.5% to 74% linear in 24 h (Maennel), and PEGDA J rises from about 4-5 at 1 kDa to about 17-36 at 5.85 kDa.
claims.source_says: TPGDA-based resins showed the lowest swelling ratio with less than 0.5% over a period of 24 h in PBS. ... RC5 exhibiting a swelling ratio of 74.1%.
claims.note: The J values match Table 2 exactly (5.5-4.2, 8.9-6.9, 35.7-16.9), but the 74.1% was reported for water, not the PBS/24 h condition the claim implies.

claims.claim: By the project's f(m,n), a kPa-to-MPa hydrogel on a GPa Formlabs resin needs a hydrogel 15-725 times thicker than the stiff layer to reach the 1.5 ceiling.
claims.source_says: calcs.py section 9 output: GelMA 19 kPa on Rigid 10K m*=725.48; on Clear V5 m*=380.44; PEGDMA-600 13 MPa on Clear V5 m*=14.54, on Rigid 10K m*=27.72.
claims.note: The script arithmetic reproduces (m*=n^-1/2, 14.5 to 725), but it rests on the project's own f(m,n) and unverified moduli, and 'mechanically dead' is a modelled result, not a measured one.

overall: Three of the four key claims are supported by the sources or the script output. The Maennel swelling range is only partly right because 74.1% was measured in water, not PBS. The thickness-ratio claim is an internal calculation that reproduces but is not source-measured. No [held-out clade] or holdout material came up.
